title.narrative: Activity under preparation Support to the National Public Health Institute

description.narrative:
1.Zimbabwe is in the process of establishing a National Public Health Institute (NPHI). Zimbabwe will utilize the Africa CDC Framework for developing NPHIs. The development of a NPHI is proposed within the framework of the Global Gateway Health Package presented at the 6th EU-AU Summit in 2022. It operationalizes INTPA¿s contribution to the Team Europe Initiative on supporting National Public Health Institutes (NPHIs) in Sub Saharan Africa (SSA) that has support from ten EU MS. The TEI aims to contribute to the population¿s health and wellbeing (SDG 3) via the provision of essential public health services by NPHIs.

2.The Zimbabwe PHI will ensure its primary focus is on science and evidence generation while not being involved in service delivery. The NPHI will implement the Core Public Health Functions in line with the core mandate and functions of the MoHCC and in accordance with the directives enshrined in the Public Health Act.

3.Within the first four years and with catalytic funding from the EU, the NPHI will place its priority on: (a). Establishing the NPHI including developing its strategy and roadmap, (b) Enhancing NPHI Participation in Regional and International Networking, (c) Enhancing NPHI Digital Health Literacy and Reducing the Digital Health Skills Gap. Specific activities and associated outputs for each of the objectives are detailed in Annex 1.

4.The NPHI establishment process will run concurrently with key interventions addressing the rapidly growing Non-Communicable Diseases (NCD) burden (particularly hypertension and diabetes) in Zimbabwe[1]. It will initially prioritize NCDs primarily focusing on surveillance of NCDs, NCD Health workforce development health promotion, and information generation, research, and policy dialogue. Additional priority areas will be social science research into the cost of health promotion activities i.e., risk factors for NCDs ¿ addiction, poor diet, physical inactivity in both communities and schools.Social mobilization efforts will be undertaken to channel messages for disease prevention and health promotion. Priority is given to the NCDs due to the urgent need to strengthen the surveillance system for NCDs. The last WHO prevalence of NCD survey was conducted in 2005 in Zimbabwe. This means there is an almost 20-year gap in availability of plausible evidence to guide policy review and appropriate strategic programming.

5.The process of establishing the NPHI will be highly consultative and will begin with formulating a Multi-disciplinary Steering Committee (SC) which will lead the strategic focus and governance of the Institute and harmonization of the legislative framework. The SC will also facilitate foundational aspects including the formulation of the NPHI Strategic Plan.


[1] This EU regional action does not support strengthening PPR and laboratory networks, because these activities are funded under different funds e.g. the Pandemic Fund.
